title: Coffman's four deadlock conditions — mutual exclusion, hold-and-wait, no preemption, circular wait
shortTitle: Coffman's four deadlock conditions — mutual exclusion, hold-and-wait, no preemption, circular wait

s1_definition.profdef: Edward Coffman (1971) identified FOUR conditions that must ALL hold simultaneously for a deadlock to occur: (1) **Mutual exclusion** — the resource (lock) can be held by only ONE thread at a time. (2) **Hold and wait** — a thread HOLDS at least one lock while WAITING to acquire another. (3) **No preemption** — a lock cannot be forcibly taken from a thread; only the holding thread can release it. (4) **Circular wait** — a chain of threads exists where each waits for a lock held by the next in the chain, forming a CYCLE. If ANY ONE condition is broken, deadlock is IMPOSSIBLE. The most practical to break is **circular wait** — enforce a global ordering on all locks and require every thread to acquire locks in that order.
s1_definition.analogy: Four things must ALL be true for two tellers to deadlock at the vaults: (1) **Mutual exclusion** — only one person fits inside a vault at a time. (2) **Hold and wait** — a teller stands inside Vault-A while reaching for Vault-B's door handle. (3) **No preemption** — the manager can't drag a teller out of the vault by force. (4) **Circular wait** — Teller-1 is in Vault-A wanting Vault-B. Teller-2 is in Vault-B wanting Vault-A. A circle. Break ANY one: no deadlock. Easiest: vault rule — "always enter the lower-numbered vault FIRST." No circle possible.
s1_definition.oneliner: ALL four must be true: mutual exclusion + hold-and-wait + no preemption + circular wait. Break ANY ONE → deadlock impossible. Easiest: break circular wait via global lock ordering.
s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** Edward Coffman (1971) identified FOUR conditions that must ALL hold simultaneously for a deadlock to occur: (1) **Mutual exclusion** — the resource (lock) can be held by only ONE thread at a time. (2) **Hold and wait** — a thread HOLDS at least one lock while WAITING to acquire another. (4) **Circular wait** — a chain of threads exists where each waits for a lock held by the next in the chain, forming a CYCLE. If ANY ONE condition is broken, deadlock is IMPOSSIBLE. The most practical to break is **circular wait** — enforce a global ordering on all locks and require every thread to acquire locks in that order.

**In simple words (banking analogy):** Four things must ALL be true for two tellers to deadlock at the vaults: (1) **Mutual exclusion** — only one person fits inside a vault at a time. (2) **Hold and wait** — a teller stands inside Vault-A while reaching for Vault-B's door handle. (3) **No preemption** — the manager can't drag a teller out of the vault by force. (4) **Circular wait** — Teller-1 is in Vault-A wanting Vault-B. Teller-2 is in Vault-B wanting Vault-A. A circle. Break ANY one: no deadlock. Easiest: vault rule — "always enter the lower-numbered vault FIRST." No circle possible.

**One line to remember:** ALL four must be true: mutual exclusion + hold-and-wait + no preemption + circular wait. Break ANY ONE → deadlock impossible. Easiest: break circular wait via global lock ordering.

sections.s3_banking: **Problem — The bank's wire transfer system had complex multi-account transfers** locking 3-4 accounts per transaction. Without ordering: 4-way deadlocks occurred. With 200 threads, deadlock probability was ~5% during peak hours. Fix: all accounts sorted by account ID before locking. Lock acquired in sorted order. Circular wait impossible regardless of how many accounts are involved. Deadlock probability: 0%. Additionally: tryLock(5s) as a safety net — if ordering has a bug, timeout prevents permanent hang.

sections.s5_journey:
**Step 1.** 50 threads perform multi-account transfers between 3 accounts (A, B, C) in various combinations.

**Step 2.** Each thread sorts the involved accounts by ID before locking. Thread transferring C→A: sorts to [A, C] → locks A first, then C. Thread transferring A→B: sorts to [A, B] → locks A first, then B.

**Step 3.** No circular wait possible: every thread acquires locks in the SAME global order (alphabetical). If Thread-1 holds A and needs C, Thread-2 can't hold C and need A — Thread-2 would have locked A first (before C) in the sorted order.

**Step 4.** All 50 threads complete. Total money: 300,000 (100K × 3) — conserved. Zero deadlocks.
sections.s5b_flow:
```
  ═══ COFFMAN'S FOUR CONDITIONS ═══

  ALL FOUR must be TRUE for deadlock:
  ┌─────────────────────┐
  │ 1. Mutual Exclusion │ → locks are exclusive
  │ 2. Hold and Wait    │ → hold one, wait for another
  │ 3. No Preemption    │ → can't force-take locks
  │ 4. Circular Wait    │ → A→B→A cycle
  └─────────────────────┘
  Break ANY ONE → deadlock IMPOSSIBLE!

  ═══ HOW TO BREAK EACH ═══
  #1 Mutual Exclusion → ReadWriteLock (shared reads), lock-free (Atomic)
  #2 Hold and Wait    → tryLock both-or-none, release before retry
  #3 No Preemption    → tryLock(timeout) — give up voluntarily
  #4 Circular Wait    → GLOBAL LOCK ORDERING (sort by ID) ✅ EASIEST!

  ═══ LOCK ORDERING FOR 3 ACCOUNTS ═══
  Transfer C→A: sort → lock(A) → lock(C) → transfer → unlock
  Transfer A→B: sort → lock(A) → lock(B) → transfer → unlock
  Transfer B→C: sort → lock(B) → lock(C) → transfer → unlock
  No cycle possible! A→B→C is always the order.
```
sections.s5c_hld:
```
  ═══ HLD — Deadlock-Free Multi-Account Transfer ═══

  ┌──────────┐  REST   ┌─────────────────────────────────┐
  │ Clients  │────────→│  Transfer Service (200 threads)  │
  └──────────┘         │                                   │
                       │  transfer(accounts[], amounts[]): │
                       │  1. Sort accounts by ID           │
                       │  2. Lock all in sorted order      │
                       │  3. Apply debits + credits        │
                       │  4. Unlock in reverse order       │
                       │  → Circular wait IMPOSSIBLE!      │
                       │                                   │
                       │  Fallback: tryLock(5s timeout)    │
                       │  Monitor: findDeadlockedThreads() │
                       └───────────────────────────────────┘
```
sections.s5d_lld:
```
  ═══ LLD — Breaking Each Coffman Condition ═══

  ┌─ Break #4: Circular Wait (PREFERRED) ────────────┐
  │  multiAccountTransfer(accounts):                  │
  │    sorted = accounts.sort(by ID)                  │
  │    for a in sorted: a.lock.lock()                 │
  │    try { apply transfers }                        │
  │    finally { for a in reverse: a.lock.unlock() }  │
  │  Global order → no cycle → no deadlock!           │
  └───────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  ┌─ Break #2: Hold and Wait ────────────────────────┐
  │  tryTransfer(from, to):                           │
  │    gotFrom = from.lock.tryLock(100ms)             │
  │    gotTo = to.lock.tryLock(100ms)                 │
  │    if (gotFrom && gotTo) → transfer               │
  │    else → release all, retry                       │
  │  Never HOLD one while WAITING for another!        │
  └───────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  ┌─ Break #1: Mutual Exclusion ─────────────────────┐
  │  AtomicInteger balance                            │
  │  balance.addAndGet(-amount) → CAS, no lock!       │
  │  No lock → no mutual exclusion → no deadlock!     │
  └───────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  ┌─ Break #3: No Preemption ────────────────────────┐
  │  lock.tryLock(5, SECONDS)                         │
  │  Timeout → give up (voluntary "preemption")       │
  └───────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Coffman's four conditions for deadlock (1971): mutual exclusion (locks are exclusive), hold-and-wait (hold one lock while waiting for another), no preemption (can't forcibly take locks), and circular wait (cycle of threads waiting for each other's locks). ALL four must be true simultaneously. Breaking ANY single condition makes deadlock impossible.

The most practical to break is CIRCULAR WAIT via global lock ordering — assign a deterministic order to all locks (by account ID, object hash, or any consistent comparator) and require every thread to acquire locks in that order. For multi-account banking transfers: sort accounts by ID, lock in sorted order. Transfer A→C and C→A both lock in order [A, C] — no circle, no deadlock. Secondary strategies: tryLock (break hold-and-wait — acquire all or none), tryLock with timeout (break no-preemption — give up voluntarily), lock-free AtomicInteger/ConcurrentHashMap (break mutual exclusion — no locks at all). In production: use lock ordering as primary prevention, tryLock as safety net, and deadlock monitoring as last-line detection.
